A game-playing agent emits control actions in an environment and never assesses others' learning needs or delivers instruction, so it does not perform the activity even at the level-2 anchor of giving brief procedural instructions.

The system solves formal reasoning problems in isolation and has no agency over, communication with, or scheduling authority over group members, so it performs no coordination even at the shift-change level.

It can only answer questions grounded in a passage handed to it — enough to relay a simple procedural instruction extracted from a document, but it never identifies learners' educational needs, sequences material, or delivers and adapts instruction, so nothing at or above the level-4 'teach a course' anchor is in reach.
A game-playing agent acts on in-game controls and has no channel or function for representing an organization to customers, the public, or media, so it performs none of this activity.
The system derives answers to formal problems and has no persistent social role, memory of counterparties, or relationship-building function beyond incidental conversational politeness.
